extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for FMCSA medical exemptions (drivers), motor carriers, stakeholders, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal criteria for evaluating, publishing, renewing, and revoking exemptions from the FMCSA hearing qualification requirement for interstate commercial motor vehicle (CMV) drivers. Applies to FMCSA staff, exemption applicants, and members of the public submitting or reviewing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for exemption requests
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA must publish a notice of each exemption request in the Federal Register (49 CFR 381.315(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency must publish a notice of each exemption request in the Federal Register (49 CFR 381.315(a)). The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analysis. The Agency must provide an opportunity for public comment on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to application materials and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The public must be given an opportunity to inspect application information (including the applicant's safety analysis) and to submit comments; comments are posted to regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view comments, go to www.regulations.gov. Insert the docket number ... sort the results ... choose the first notice listed, and click 'Browse Comments.' If you do not have access to the internet, you may view the docket online by visiting Dockets Operations. DOT posts these comments, including any personal information the commenter provides, to www.regulations.gov, as described in DOT/ALL-14 FDMS. The comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory safety-equivalence standard for granting exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA must determine whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption (49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency reviews the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted and determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved by complying with the regulation, pursuant to the standard set forth in 49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content when exemption is granted or denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision from which the applicant will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)); if denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision from which the applicant will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)). If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of medical exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical exemptions may be renewed and FMCSA issues medical exemptions for a 2-year period to align with the maximum duration of a driver's medical certification (49 CFR 381.300(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption may be renewed (49 CFR 381.300(b)). FMCSA grants medical exemptions from the FMCSRs for a 2-year period to align with the maximum duration of a driver's medical certification. Each exemption will be valid for 2 years from the effective date unless revoked earlier by FMCSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for revocation of an exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption will be revoked if: (1) the person fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the exemption; (2) the exemption has resulted in a lower level of safety than was maintained prior to being granted; or (3) continuation of the exemption would not be consistent with the goals and objectives of 49 U.S.C. 31136, 49 U.S.C. chapter 313, or the FMCSRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption will be revoked if the following occurs: (1) the person fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the exemption; (2) the exemption has resulted in a lower level of safety than was maintained prior to being granted; or (3) continuation of the exemption would not be consistent with the goals and objectives of 49 U.S.C. 31136, 49 U.S.C. chapter 313, or the FMCSRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing physical qualification standard (§391.41(b)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is physically qualified to drive a CMV if that person first perceives a forced whispered voice in the better ear at not less than 5 feet with or without the use of a hearing aid or, if tested by use of an audiometric device, does not have an average hearing loss in the better ear greater than 40 decibels at 500 Hz, 1,000 Hz, and 2,000 Hz with or without a hearing aid when the audiometric device is calibrated to American National Standard Z24.5—1951.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard was adopted in 1970 and was revised in 1971 to allow drivers to be qualified under this standard while wearing a hearing aid (35 FR 6458, 6463 (Apr. 22, 1970) and 36 FR 12857 (July 8, 1971)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption during exemption period
rubrics_metrics.description: While an exemption is in effect, no State may enforce any law or regulation that conflicts with the exemption with respect to the person operating under the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the period the exemption is in effect, no State shall enforce any law or regulation that conflicts with this exemption with respect to a person operating under the exemption.
